title: How Much Fiber in Blueberries? 3.6g per Cup
description: Blueberries: about 3.6 g of fiber per 1 cup (13% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in blueberries?
intro: Blueberries rank #7 of 15 fruits on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in blueberries by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in blueberries?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists blueberries, raw at 2.4 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup; 148 g) therefore has about 3.6 g of fiber and 84 calories. That is 13% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 14% of a 25 g day and 9% of a 38 g day.
Blueberries are popular for their color and convenience, but on fiber they sit in the middle of the berry range: more than strawberries, well below raspberries and blackberries.

sections.heading: Wild vs cultivated blueberries
paragraphs: Wild (lowbush) blueberries are smaller and are mostly sold frozen. Because more berries fit in a cup, labels for wild blueberries often list somewhat more fiber per cup than USDA’s cultivated blueberry entry. Use the label if you buy wild.
Dried blueberries and blueberry muffins are much less helpful: dried berries are usually sweetened, and muffins contain only a handful of berries.

sections.heading: How blueberries compare with other fruits
paragraphs: Of the 15 fruits on this site, blueberries rank #7 for fiber per typical serving and #9 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 4.2 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [dried figs](/fiber-in-dried-figs) at 3.6 g (1/4 cup); [prunes](/fiber-in-prunes) at 3.4 g (5 prunes); [orange](/fiber-in-orange) at 3.1 g (1 medium). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), blueberries are #29 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding blueberries to your day
paragraphs: Mix blueberries with a higher-fiber berry or add them to a base that already has fiber, such as oatmeal or a bran cereal.

Example: 1 cup blueberries, 1 cup oatmeal, 2 tbsp walnuts. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 8.6 g of fiber, with 3.6 g from the blueberries. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of blueberries?
faqs.a: 2.4 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Blueberries, raw). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in blueberries (1/2 cup)?
faqs.a: About 1.8 g, for 74 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.
Moderately. One cup is about 3.6 g (1 cup), about 13% of the Daily Value.
Raspberries have a little over twice as much per cup: about 8 g (1 cup).
